title: The ALMaQUEST Survey. XII. Dense Molecular Gas as Traced by HCN and HCO<SUP>+</SUP> in Green Valley Galaxies
question: Is the low molecular-gas star formation efficiency of green valley galaxies (relative to main sequence galaxies with similar CO-traced molecular gas fractions) due to a lack of dense gas (f_dense) or to a low star formation efficiency of the dense gas (SFE_dense)?

data.sensitivity: Line cube rms ~0.087 to 0.152 mJy/beam (channels binned to 30-50 km/s)

what.value: Global stellar mass and SFR of the 5 targets (Table 1) from the Pipe3D value-added catalog

evidence.quote: Values are taken from value-added catalog (cite: san18) in the SDSS DR15 release (cite: aqu19).

what.value: CO(1-0) data reduction, maps and spectra from the ALMaQUEST survey

evidence.quote: Details on the CO(1-0) data reduction and properties are described in the main survey paper (cite: lin20)
The CO spectra from the previous program (cite: lin20) are also overplotted for comparison.

what.value: EMPIRE resolved HCN/HCO+/CO and SFR measurements (9 galaxies) compared in the dense-gas SK relation

evidence.quote: we also plot the EMPIRE sample (magenta points), which consists of 9 galaxies with resolved measurements ($\sim$1-2 kpc scale resolution) from (cite: jim19)

what.value: Literature global SFR and gas luminosities for post-starburst, early-type, star-forming, starburst galaxies and star-forming subregions (Figures 12-13)

evidence.loc: 4.2 Comparison with previous studies in the literature
evidence.quote: including EMPIRE galaxies (cite: jim19), post-starburst galaxies (cite: row15; fre18; fre23), early-type galaxies (cite: cro12), star-forming and starbursting galaxies (cite: gao04), and subregions in star-forming galaxies (cite: use15)

external_data.citation: (cite: jim19); (cite: row15; fre18; fre23); (cite: cro12); (cite: gao04); (cite: use15)

what.value: Metallicity diagnostic (O3N2) used to justify fixed conversion factors

evidence.quote: the spaxel-based metallicities, computed using the O3N2 diagnostic (cite: pet04; kew08), exhibit median values ranging from 8.69 to 8.76 for each galaxy

recipe.method: tclean with Briggs weighting, user-specified image center, 0.5 arcsec pixels and a 2.5 arcsec restoring beam to match MaNGA; lines imaged separately; channels binned to 30-50 km/s

recipe.goal: Build integrated intensity maps and total line intensities
recipe.method: immoments on the cubes, integrating a hand-set velocity range without clipping; total intensities from summing spaxels within 1.5 Re
key_parameters: velocity range set by hand to match the line profile, no clipping
1.5 Re aperture from the Pipe3D catalog

recipe.goal: Convert line luminosities to gas masses
recipe.method: Constant alpha_CO for CO and constant alpha_HCN and alpha_HCO+ for the dense gas
assumptions: alpha_CO = 4.35 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1, includes helium and heavier elements
alpha_HCN = alpha_HCO+ = 10 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1, fixed because dense-gas conversion factors are unexplored at kpc scales
Fixed factor fair because metallicity within 0.07 dex of solar

recipe.goal: Derive spaxel SFR and stellar mass surface densities from MaNGA
recipe.method: Pipe3D value-added products; Balmer-decrement extinction correction, Halpha-to-SFR (Kennicutt 1998, Salpeter IMF), per-spaxel normalisation by inclination-corrected physical area
assumptions: intrinsic H-alpha/H-beta = 2.86, Milky Way extinction curve with Rv = 3.1
H-alpha in star-forming spaxels is purely from star formation; SFR in retired spaxels is an upper limit

recipe.goal: Apply S/N cuts and classify spaxels
recipe.method: S/N cuts on emission lines, BPT classification, and Halpha EW cuts to define star-forming, retired and other spaxels
key_parameters: S/N > 3 for H-alpha and H-beta, > 2 for [OIII] and [NII], > 2.5 for CO, HCN, HCO+
retired: H-alpha EW < 3 A and S/N > 3 in H-alpha

recipe.goal: Resolved relations: dense-gas SK relation, SFE_mol vs f_dense and SFE_dense, sSFR dependences
recipe.method: Spaxel-by-spaxel Pearson correlations for all spaxel types, ODR fit of the star-forming spaxels of 7815-12705 as reference line, comparison with EMPIRE; sSFR decomposed into SFE x f_dense x f_mol

recipe.goal: Test for artificial correlations from shared denominators/numerators
recipe.method: Generate synthetic datasets by shuffling Sigma_mol and Sigma_dense (and Sigma_mol and Sigma_SFR), 500 trials each; repeat on the central half of the Sigma_SFR range
key_parameters: 500 trials; Sigma_SFR range -3 < log10 Sigma_SFR < -1.5 for the restricted test

recipe.goal: Check S/N effects and compare global properties with literature samples
recipe.method: Repeat SK correlations with an upper S/N(CO) limit of 10; compare global SFR vs L_CO/L_HCN/L_HCO+ and L_HCN/L_CO with literature samples

score_reason: ALMA program code, band, configuration, tclean robust/pixel/beam, alpha factors, S/N and EW cuts and Table 2 numbers are given, but calibration details, masks, line-free channels, velocity ranges, regridding and the CO/MaNGA data processing are not, and many results exist only in figures.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA Band 3 data and MaNGA/Pipe3D catalog are survey/archive products with a project code given, the imaging recipe is mostly specified, and the main results (integrated intensities, luminosities, Pearson r, shuffling tests) are numeric; CO data from ALMaQUEST must be fetched separately.
